name: Koa
description: Koa is a regional Southeast Asian variant in the Ceki family using matching and sequence construction with Ceki cards.

content.text: Koa is a regional Southeast Asian variant in the Ceki family using matching and sequence construction with Ceki cards.

Dates back to the Qing Dynasty. Money cards (divided into Coins, Strings, and Myriads) were the direct ancestors of modern Mahjong tiles. Quan Dui evolved as a faster, pair-focused variant of the more complex 'Guan Pai' games.
Ceki/Cherki deck traditionally used in Peranakan card play, typically 60 cards per head deck.

Dealer gets 16 cards, others get 15. Counter-clockwise play.

items.text: Quan Dui double stake: When the winner has all eight pairs as Dui (identical cards), they collect double the agreed stake from each opponent.

Optional win claim: With eight pairs of mixed Ka and Dui, the player may choose to continue playing for quan dui instead of claiming; if the final pair was claimed from the discard as Ka, they must expose and win single stake.
